reviews.text: Soulbound: Online is a fun mix of an MMO and a roguelite. Every dungeon feels different because of different ability and relic combinations. I also enjoy the profession skills like hacking, foraging, fishing, and mining. The classless system allows me change my build anytime, which makes the game fun to experiment with. Since, the game in Early Access, I have run into server issues, but that's expected. The team has been quick to fix issues and listens to player feedback, which is great to see. The core gameplay is already fun. If you enjoy grinding for gear, trying different builds, customizing your abilities, relics, and cosmetics, and play with friends, I think it's worth checking out.

A roguelike MMORPG is a really great idea, and it's genuinely fun to play. The server problems from day one have been resolved. The studio did some questionable things with crypto and NFTs, but the game itself is clean. There will be an in-game shop and a premium pass, but according to the developers, nothing will be pay-to-win. The stamina system really isn't an issue. You have 100 stamina, and each gathering action (mining, harvesting, etc.) costs 3. When you run out, you can fully recover in a tavern in 2–3 minutes or you can craft your own meals to get virtually unlimited stamina regeneration. It also gives players who farm 24/7 a reason to take a break and let others use the farming spots. At least give it a try and make up your own mind.

As a player of former Soulbound from before the rework, I can say that there's future potential here, and the EA version with upcoming development is something to pay attention to as how it pans out. [h1]Launch Issues[/h1] The first week of EA will be rocky with usual server overloads and launch bugs, but once those get fixed, the game will really shine (as can be seen as other negative reviews that complain about launch issues <- this is still valid criticism as the infrastructure, especially under load, is far from comfortable gameplay being stuck every second doing any action). [h2]What the game is[/h2] It's a laid-back bullet haven combat mixed with roguelite dungeon runs, and gear progression farming. The art and Pixel art style is quite clean with no apparent AI use on visuals from what I gathered. Abilties are interesting but the relics (the upgrades you pick upon level up in a run) are pretty basic and only few actually change how the abilities function. The tutorial and opening hours are basically your typical quest spam, mostly there to unlock abilities (spells/your build) and new dungeons. I guess that's where the "MMO" part comes in, with quests being a core part of the progression rather than anything else, I'm not a lore guy in games usually, but the story seems pretty generic, and nothing to pay bigger attention to. The open world mostly acts as a social hub instead of a place you'll spend a ton of time fighting. It's where you run into other players, level professions, and use the housing system, which is tied directly into the crafting loop by letting you place workbenches inside your apartment. On top of that, you've got fishing, gardening, gathering, and other professions, all using a RuneScape-style 0-99 leveling system. https://i.imgur.com/wAYCELQ.png Though take the MMO label with a grain of salt here. Honestly, I dislike when devs slap the MMO tag on everything these days, but end of the day it's just semantics since everyone has a different definition anyway. The game plays more like a hub dungeon crawler, though the open world does have layered zones, trading, and scheduled map events. [h2]Content[/h2] The game features a pretty short MSQ questing campaign and some side quests (personally I didn't find anything super particularly interesting out of them and felt pretty generic), but the main gameloop revolves around running dungeons solo or in a party. Currently, here is the list of dungeons and their different difficulties available in EA: https://i.imgur.com/peL3QYy.png Whether that's a lot/not enough content is for everyone to answer on their own volition. For me, it's enough content to get like a week's worth of gaming out of it, which personally makes the price worth it. As for anyone reading this, you'll need to answer if it's worth it for yourself. [h2]Combat and Build Variety[/h2] You select up to 3 abilties + Weapon (that's your build), and then you also have gear pieces that you craft/drop from dungeons, so it's a gearing game in order to keep your character stronger https://i.imgur.com/pV2hVnI.png Each Dungeon is a fresh run from level 1, and killing monsters drops xp, upon a level you pick 1 out of 3 relics (upgrades) for your abilities, so that's where the Roguelite element kicks in. [h2]QoL[/h2] Some bank UI could use some more QoL changes, and we have yet to see an Auction House in the game as it's not present right now, but the overall UI is easy to use with explanation tooltips at most places. [h2]Balance/Difficulty[/h2] It's too early for me to judge how the game is balanced but for now I saw some people running quite broken builds trivialising even hardest dungeons currently available in EA so it's safe to assume the balancing needs lot of work and game is one of those "easier" ones in terms of difficulty. [h2]Monetisation[/h2] From what I know and now is present in the game, the devs philosophy is being anti p2w with only cosmetics that will be available in the game store (currently the game offers no MTX purchases as of EA launch) [h2]Performance[/h2] Client performance is pretty good and the FPS should be stable even on a toaster, however I did notice some memory leaks buildup over extended sessions of gameplay, so restarting the game if you're a nolifer will be part of the experience, so that's something to note. [h2]Summary[/h2] For me game is seeming fun and I can see myself playing it for time being and returning to it from time to time for what it's supposed to be but isn't anything superb and definitely won't put it near the top of my favourite games but there's fun to be had.

This review is ignoring the bugs, NFT drama(mostly) and launch day struggles. This game has three (3) main systems going for it's gameplay loop. The roguelite/bullet heaven part. The gearing/meta progression part, and the Life skills/skilling part, so let's go one by one. The core gameplay, the dungeons and bullet heaven is weak. If you played any, and I mean any vsuv clone, you've had a better experience than this. The skills themselves are okay, inoffensive, nothing special. But the upgrades and "perks" are just boring. Every dungeon feels exactly like the last, there are no upgrades who change more than slightly the way you use your skills or play, the perks feel nonexistent, and the rare moments you do find one of the very rare perks, they are just higher numbers for your skills. The enemies have some unique movement patterns, and bosses have the standard red floor mechanics, but if you're playing with anything besides 20 ping (and you will), enemies will hit you even though they missed you on your screen. And if the server lags (and it will), you insta die and lose a run. The questing is also quite weak. The lore is there, I guess. It exists for the purpose of saying it exists. None of the quests are interesting, always being some kind of fetch or kill quests. And you will be forced to do them, since some skills are locked behind completing them. And the life skills are also extremely boring. Most of them are just click and click again somewhere different 1.5 seconds after, repeat about 50 seconds and wait for stamina regen(which takes maybe 2 minutes of waiting in a tavern, or by eating food). Some have a little minigame, which after doing them for the 100th time just gets annoying. But the biggest problem with the game is that everything feels incomplete. If you want any information your best bet is asking in the discord and hoping one of the NFT era sweats answers for you. The Wiki was offline for all of day 1, but it wouldn't have been up to date anyway. Finding information inside the own game is very limited to say the least and annoying, and even some information inside the game itself is not up to date. Skills will appear to be based on one attribute in one place and another somewhere else. Quests will fail to complete and you have no choice but to open a support ticket and get it completed that way. That being said, the support team itself is a huge positive, I had two broken quests and they both got solved within 60 seconds of talking to a member of support, but that's not a great excuse for a broken game. Is it a horrible game? No it isn't, it's enjoyable, as every bullet heaven ends up being, but it only feels that way for the first 30 minutes. After that, you're doing busy work for your life skills, and seeing the same runs again and again in the dungeons, or doing quests that are just more of the other two. The selling point of roguelites, every run being different than the last, simply doesn't exist here. It lacks variety for that to be possible, and the very systems of the game work against that. Upgrading skills isn't cheap, and at some point you don't want to be using unupgraded skills, add to that gear usually having stats that work better for a class of skills rather than others, so what you end up with is a game where you've seen all it has to show in one or two hours of gameplay. You can keep pushing for better gear or higher numbers, but your experience will be the exact same. The game has potential, but it's unfinished, and it shows. Usually I wouldn't give a negative review(or a review at all) to an early access product for being unfinished, but they already got their starter cash with the NFT rug pull, and while the fact it's scammy is debatable, it's undeniable they tried their best to hide and dissociate from the old project. Before release day, the only way you could even find that out was by interacting with a dropdown in a server in their discord and receiving a private message about it(It is now pinned to the English general chat). They took steps to make sure people didn't instantly find out their past, and regardless of why, that should add scrutiny.

Games fine, lots of targeted hate from past actions that have nothing to do with the current version of the game. See for yourself, the only way to really know if a game is good is by trying it, not listening to review bias.

Not quite there yet but on the right track. While Soulbound Online emulates the Starbound art style with hints of Ragnarok Online; ultimately the game feels more focused on delivering a grindy 'survivors-style' back to back dungeon experience. The game currently feels like a mobile phone game with slow animations, movement and long cooldowns. While aiming to be helpful, the game tutorial runs the risk of losing players, assuming that the player cant even figure out basic movement or actions themselves; adding to a feeling of unnecessary task overload. Lastly, there were considerable lag spikes given the art style and also many unresponsive NPCs that took multiple clicks to activate. All in all, this game has some good foundation ideas but could benefit from more stress tests, an even wider variety of weapons and skills, varied enemy movements, and speedier animations.

The game is pretty good. The presentation is really great. Art and sound design are both on point. Music is a bit forgettable but non-offensive. Voice acting is minimal but when it's there it's serviceable. The gameplay is fun but a little shallow. Bullet heavan "dungeons" with life skilling. The combat portions are fun but a little under baked. The net code needs some work because the nit detection can be quite off. The life skilling is clunky, but if you like seeing the number go up it does the job. The stamina system takes the place of having spawn timers. Personally, I think it's not ideal but it does the job of binding in-game resources to irl time just like every mmo does. Apparently, there's some "drama" about previous games and potential monetization. All in all it seems like standard indie devs figuring things out as they go and then keyboard warriors interpreting everything in bad faith. Hopefully things improve because this game has some serious potential. They've been responding to bugs and generally active.

The game is fun if not slightly addictive. If you like crafting/farming sims and survivor like games. This is a combination of those two things. Believe it or not, the game sort of reminds me of stardew valley in a way, but without the relationships. That’s probably not a comparison most people are going to make. But, I smash rocks. Pull up plants. Farm vegetables. Manage stamina. Interact with townsfolk. And go into dungeons to gather resources. All in a pixel art game. So, nothing like stardew valley at all, but it oddly reminds me of it all the same. (Shrug) At the time of this writing I am 12 and a half hours in, and I am still discovering new things. For a game I spent ~$13 (bought on sale during release discount). This means I have already gotten an hour of gameplay per dollar, and I am likely to get many more hours. That said, the game is slightly repetitive. So far, smashing rocks, pulling up plants. Farming. Managing stamina. Interacting with townsfolk. Gather resources in dungeons. Is basically what there is to do in the game. Also crafting I guess. But despite the repetitive nature, it has continued to feel rewarding because I am still currently “progressing” so I get that continued dopamine hit from that progression. After 12+ hours of gameplay. And based on where I and what I see. I can easily see doubling that gameplay time before hitting any sort of end to that progression in the games current state. So I am enjoying it.

I don’t normally write Steam reviews, but I wanted to support the game in whatever small way I could by sharing my experience, because I’ve genuinely been enjoying it so much so far. I’ve only played a few hours, but I’m having a great time. The pixel art looks fantastic, the world feels alive, and the gameplay is a fun blend of ideas from different games. The biggest draw for me is the progression. As a longtime RuneScape player, I love working toward small goals—leveling skills to unlock better tools, gear, and crafting options. Soulbound captures that same satisfying progression loop without feeling overly complicated. The dungeons are fun and offer a different take on MMO gameplay, and the quests have been more engaging than the usual “go kill 10 monsters” style. They have a bit more variety while still being easy to follow. I also want to address the biggest criticisms. Many negative reviews came from launch day when the servers were overloaded. I played on day one, and while there were issues, the developers responded quickly by adding servers and fixing problems. By day two, my experience was smooth. I’ve also seen claims that the game is a “crypto scam.” From what I’ve seen, the developers have been transparent about the game’s history. They took a project that didn’t succeed in the crypto space and rebuilt it into a traditional Steam game. That doesn’t bother me, especially if the end result is a fun game. Overall, I’m really enjoying Soulbound so far. It’s reasonably priced, the gameplay is fun, and I’m excited to see how it grows with the roadmap the developers have shared.
